newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia parliament wants 13-20 pct budget rises.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia parliament wants 13-20 pct budget rises.

text.p: The parliamentary budget committee had proposed raising Indonesia's 1997/1998 budget by between about 13 and 20 percent to 102.3-to-108 trillion rupiah from the current 1996/1997 budget of 90 trillion rupiah, Bisnis Indonesia said on Friday.

The ruling Golkar party proposed an increase of 12.91 percent, the armed forces faction 14.5 percent, the opposition United Development Party 14 percent and the opposition Indonesian Democratic Party 20 percent, the daily reported.
The four groups proposed the increases during a meeting with Finance Minister Mar'ie Muhammad on Thursday.
They based their proposals on similar assumptions that oil prices would remain at current levels, the continuing inflow of offshore capital funds and an expected rise in tax revenues.
The meeting's chairman I Gde Artjana said the government's accounts for the first half of 1996/1997 ending September showed a surplus of 700 billion rupiah.
He said a surplus of 100 billion rupiah was also expected in the second half of the 1996/1997 fiscal year (April to March).
